The address at the top of this page already works

There is nothing to set up. Type any name you like in front of the @, choose one of the names from the list, and that address exists from that second. Fake emails sent to it show up on this page a moment later, so you can open a confirmation link or copy a code without going near your own inbox.

No sign-up, no password, no phone number. Take the address, use it, forget it. That is really all a fake email address is: an ordinary working mailbox that simply is not the one you care about.

What people use fake mail for

Almost everything comes down to five things:

  • Reading an article that hides behind a sign-up form.
  • Downloading a file that asks for an email address first.
  • Getting a one-time code from a site you will never open again.
  • Trying a service out before you give it your real inbox.
  • Testing your own sign-up form without filling your mailbox with test messages.

Three steps from address to message

  1. Copy the address at the top of the page, or type your own word in front of the @ and choose one of the names from the list.
  2. Paste it into the sign-up form, the download page or wherever the other site asks for an email.
  3. Come back to this tab and wait. The message appears here by itself.

That is the whole idea of a fake mail generator with an inbox: the address and the mailbox it belongs to sit on the same page, and you never have to log in anywhere to read what arrives.

Why give a site a fake email address at all

Most sign-up forms want your email for a single message: the confirmation. After that, the same address keeps receiving newsletters, reminders and offers you never asked for. And if that site is ever hacked, it is your real address that ends up on the leaked list.

A fake email address takes the one message you need and keeps everything that follows away from the inbox you actually read. Your own address stays for the people and services you trust.

How long it lives, and why you cannot send

A fake mail address keeps working for several days. Long enough for a confirmation that only turns up tomorrow, short enough that forgotten mailboxes do not pile up here forever.

You can receive mail here, but not send it. That is a decision, not a missing button. A free fake email generator that also lets people send becomes a spam machine within a week, and then every name it offers gets blocked everywhere. Receiving keeps working precisely because sending stays closed.

If you want an address that lasts longer

You can put your own name on it instead of ours. If you already own a website name (the kind you pay a few dollars a year for), you can send its mail here by adding one MX record where you bought it. The guide shows exactly what to type. After that the mailbox lasts as long as your name does, and since nobody else uses it, no list can block it.

Common questions

Is it really free?

Yes. No paid version, no limit on how many addresses you take, and nothing to fill in before you get one.

Can anyone else read my mail?

Yes, and it is worth knowing. An address here has no password, so anyone who types the same address sees the same mailbox. Fine for a sign-up code. Wrong place for anything you would not want a stranger to read.

Can I come back to the same address tomorrow?

While it is still alive, yes. Type it in again and the mailbox is where you left it. Just do not build anything permanent on a mailbox meant to expire.

Do I need to keep refreshing the page?

No. New messages show up in this tab on their own, a moment after they are sent. Just keep the page open while you wait.

Does this work for Gmail?

An address made here is not a Google account and cannot pass for one. What people usually mean by that question is answered in the Fake Gmail Generator article.
